offers_products.reason: Sells NERLYNX (neratinib) oral cancer tablets; develops alisertib.

offers_services.reason: Revenue comes from drug sales and licensing; no services to customers are offered as a main business.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Breast cancer patients take NERLYNX tablets, and prescribing doctors choose it for them. Patients are the end recipients.

sells_to_organizations.reason: NERLYNX is sold through specialty pharmacies and distributors, and licensed to partners abroad.

recurring_revenue.reason: NERLYNX is a daily oral cancer therapy, so patients refill it repeatedly over months.

cyclical_demand.reason: Cancer treatment is medically necessary and cannot easily be postponed in a downturn.

big_ticket.reason: Monthly prescription fills of oral tablets are small, frequent purchases.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for a patented drug product, not staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main buyers are large specialty pharmacy distributors and licensing partners, with payers behind them.

asset_heavy.reason: In-licenses drug candidates and outsources manufacturing; mainly needs R&D spending, not plants or fleets.

notes: Buyer classification is uncertain: patients receive the drug, while distributors and partners purchase it.
